annotations.text:
Same screen, three aesthetics.
Collections desk for an Indian lender — voice agent calls borrowers in Hindi/Tamil/Marathi about overdue EMIs.
Identical data in all three so the comparison is fair.

A — KHATA
The traditional Indian ledger: buff paper, lac red, ruled lines instead of cards. A collections book is a khata, so the product looks like one.

For: distinctive, calm to read for hours, rules encode structure without boxing everything.
Against: light UI is unusual for an ops tool; risks reading as nostalgic if pushed further.

B — SWITCHBOARD
Telephony operations. Sodium-lamp amber on near-black, mono throughout, live waveform per call.

For: highest density, reads as serious infrastructure, the waveform makes it unmistakably a voice product.
Against: closest to a conventional dark dashboard — the safe choice, and the least memorable.

C — SIGNAL
The borrower's own sentence is the headline, set large in its own script. Editorial: Bodoni, deep black band, one vermilion accent.

For: puts the thing no call centre gives you — what the borrower actually said — at the centre. Most striking in a demo.
Against: lowest density; a manager wanting 50 rows at a glance will fight it.
